run.question: We got a customer complaint about slow response times in Europe. The customer mentioned seeing request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 in their error page. Find what happened with this request and which service had the issue.

report.summary: The request ID resolves to exactly one log record in the Elasticsearch log store: at 2026-11-18T13:35:47Z the auth service in region eu-west handled POST /api/v2/auth/validate for user customer-39284 and logged ERROR 'Authentication request timeout - request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 took 15847ms to respond. LDAP backend connection pool exhausted. Customer authentication failed after retry attempts.' (response_time_ms 15847). The sampled baseline for the same auth service is 150 ms on every INFO record across all six regions between 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-23, so this response was roughly 105x that baseline. The service that had the issue is therefore auth in eu-west, and its own error text attributes the failure to exhaustion of its LDAP backend connection pool. The problem was not a Europe-wide slowdown: eu-central and every other region/service in the store show a 150 ms maximum, and the whole store contains only this one ERROR record. The LDAP backend itself is outside every source observable in this Run (no LDAP service, workload, index or config; Prometheus and Jaeger failed for every query; the Kubernetes cluster is younger than the incident), so the LDAP-side origin cannot be independently confirmed.

claims.text: Search for REQ-EU-8K4M2 across all 1620 indices over the authorized window (2026-10-24T16:14:14Z..2026-11-23T16:14:14Z) returned exactly one document: index app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05, @timestamp 2026-11-18T13:35:47Z, service 'auth', region 'eu-west', endpoint '/api/v2/auth/validate', level ERROR, response_time_ms 15847, user_id 'customer-39284', message 'Authentication request timeout - request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 took 15847ms to respond. LDAP backend connection pool exhausted. Customer authentication failed after retry attempts.'

Across the whole authorized window the geo log store holds 1621 documents: 1620 at level INFO and 1 at level ERROR; the ERROR bucket contains only the auth/eu-west record, and eu-west has 271 documents versus 270 for each of ap-northeast, ap-south, eu-central, us-east and us-west.

The auth service's sampled baseline is 150 ms: all 60 INFO auth documents (6 regions x 10 sampled days, 2026-11-14T16:12:00Z to 2026-11-23T16:12:00Z) carry response_time_ms 150, including eu-west on 2026-11-18T16:12:00Z, while the single ERROR document at 2026-11-18T13:35:47Z carries 15847 ms.

Response-time statistics by region and by service show eu-west max 15847 ms (avg 207.92, 271 docs) and all other regions max 150 ms; only service 'auth' exceeds 150 ms (max 15847, avg 407.33, 61 docs), while each of the other 26 services has max 150 ms over 60 docs.

A dedicated ERROR-level aggregation over app-185-geo-* for 2026-11-18T12:00:00Z..2026-11-18T15:00:00Z returned exactly one document, bucketed by service 'auth', region 'eu-west' and the single message about request REQ-EU-8K4M2 timing out at 15847 ms with the LDAP backend connection pool exhausted.

The auth service's own error record attributes the 15847 ms response and the failed customer authentication to exhaustion of its LDAP backend connection pool, so the fault surfaces in the auth service and its named dependency is the LDAP backend.

Queries for 'LDAP' and for '"connection pool" OR "customer-39284" OR "timeout"' across all 1620 indices over the authorized window each returned only the same single auth/eu-west ERROR document; no other LDAP- or timeout-related log record was returned.

The Kubernetes cluster contains 24 deployments and 29 services, including ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping and valkey-cart; neither the deployment nor the Service inventory contains an object named auth or an object named ldap, so the auth service and its LDAP backend have no workload or Service object in this cluster at query time.

The only fault-injection configuration found is otel-demo ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json); every flag in it (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad) has defaultVariant 'off', and none references auth, LDAP or European auth latency.

All 32 pods in the cluster started between 2026-11-23T14:36:08Z and 2026-11-23T14:38:05Z with restartCount 0, i.e. the cluster is younger than the 2026-11-18 incident and cannot describe cluster state at that time.

A Europe-wide regional slowdown is not supported: eu-central's maximum response_time_ms is 150 over 270 documents and only the single eu-west auth record exceeds 150 ms; eu-west's elevated average (207.92) is caused entirely by that one 15847 ms record.

An otel-demo feature-flag fault injection is not a plausible cause for this request: the flagd-config flags are all off by default and none targets an auth/LDAP path, and no auth workload exists in the cluster those flags apply to.

The 15847 ms auth response was caused by exhaustion of the auth service's LDAP backend connection pool, as its own error text states; the LDAP backend is outside every observable source in this Run, so whether it was overloaded, misconfigured or restarted cannot be confirmed.

No cluster-side object can corroborate the auth log: the deployment and Service inventories read at query time contain neither an auth nor an ldap object, so there is no Kubernetes workload or Service whose state would show the auth service or its LDAP dependency failing during the incident.

gaps: Prometheus is unreachable: every PromQL call in this Run failed with status error / SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (get_label_values for service_name on traces_span_metrics_calls_total, get_metric_names for traces_.*, execute_prometheus_instant_query 'up', get_prometheus_target job otel-collector). No metric evidence exists for auth or for any latency/error rate, so metric state is unknown, not zero.

Jaeger is unreachable: traces_list_services failed twice and traces_search for service frontend at 2026-11-18T13:00-14:00Z failed, all with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no trace of request REQ-EU-8K4M2 or of the auth service could be retrieved.

The Elasticsearch store contains no LDAP backend telemetry: it holds app-185-geo-* indices only for analytics, api, auth, billing, cache, cart, catalog, checkout, db, inventory, notification, orders, payments, pricing, profiles, promotions, ratings, recommendations, reviews, search, shipping, subscriptions, tracking, users, web, wishlist and worker, and queries for index patterns logs-* and otel-* returned no indices. The connection-pool exhaustion stated in the auth message therefore cannot be verified at the LDAP side.

Log coverage is sparse: the store returns one document per service/region/day (1620 INFO documents for 27 services x 6 regions x 10 days), so request rate, error rate and latency distribution around 2026-11-18T13:35:47Z are unknown; only one eu-west auth sample per day is visible, and a second eu-west auth document dated 2026-11-18T16:12:00Z shows 150 ms, so the duration and blast radius of the degradation are unknown.

The Kubernetes events query over all namespaces returned no_data with 0 items processed, so any change, restart or rollout around 2026-11-18 is unknown; events may simply have expired. An earlier search for REQ-EU-8K4M2 restricted to the default one-hour window also returned no_data before the full authorized window found the record.
The Kubernetes cluster cannot describe the incident period: all pods started 2026-11-23T14:36-14:38 (after the 2026-11-18 event) and the API objects are point-in-time only.

The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so no deployment, configuration or infrastructure change record for the auth service or its LDAP backend around 2026-11-18 could be checked.
Secrets could not be read, so any LDAP connection-pool size, host or credential setting that might explain the exhaustion could not be verified.
next_steps: Inspect the auth service's LDAP connection-pool configuration (pool size, acquire timeout, max wait) and the LDAP backend's own health, connection counts and logs around 2026-11-18T13:35Z, using a source that carries LDAP telemetry (not available in this Run).

Pull the full request trace for REQ-EU-8K4M2 and auth service metrics (latency, error rate, connection-pool saturation) once Jaeger and Prometheus are reachable, to confirm whether the 15847 ms timeout was isolated or part of a burst.
Check change history for the auth service and its LDAP backend around 2026-11-18 for configuration, pool-size or infrastructure changes that could have exhausted the connection pool.
Confirm with the customer's provider whether other European requests, especially eu-west auth calls, failed at the same time, since the log store here shows only one error document.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

notes: The tool filtered @timestamp to the query window; this filter cannot be turned off.
